response.description: A corrected GRU4Rec cold start for the matched RecHarness Amazon benchmark. Train one independent GRU-based sequential recommender for each of four categories: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Select improvements using macro-average validation HR@10 while preserving the GRU4Rec backbone and fixed evaluation protocol.
response.motivation: Provide a reproducible starting point for measuring improvements within the GRU4Rec family. Fixed splits, seeds, candidate sampling, and category routing make validation comparisons consistent. No paper, implementation, or measured results were supplied.
response.implementation_notes: Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42, with at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Read data through os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Histories are left padded, so read the final nonpadding position rather than count-1. Maintain exactly one trained model/checkpoint per category, with matching embedded predictor architecture. Preserve ModelView compatibility and the required DiagnosisProbe and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt interfaces. Use only available public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Keep training single-GPU and within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. The host independently evaluates validation HR@10 using 200 users per category and 99 unique negatives with seed 42; hidden test data remains excluded.
response.pseudocode:
Set preprocessing_seed = 0 and training_seed = 42
For each of the four required categories:
    Load the supplied fixed splits from GAGC_DATA_DIR
    Initialize the supplied corrected GRU4Rec model
    Train one model within 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch
    Extract sequence features at the final nonpadding position
    Save one selected checkpoint and its matching architecture configuration
Write working/predict.py with category routing and matching model definitions
Preserve family-compatible diagnostic interfaces
Submit artifacts for independent host validation
Compare trials by macro-average validation HR@10

originality.positive: Establishes explicit family-specific correctness and reproducibility requirements.
originality.negative: Describes a controlled baseline protocol rather than a new modeling contribution.

future_potential.positive: Supports controlled exploration of jointly trained GRU layers, losses, sampling strategies, and optimization settings.
future_potential.negative: No supplied results establish improvement, and the fixed compute budget limits experimentation.

code_difficulty.positive: Independent category training and GRU sequence modeling are straightforward implementation patterns.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding correctness, diagnostic compatibility, and checkpoint–predictor consistency require careful integration; the actual baseline code was not supplied.
